title: Separation techniques

explain.say: Today we will learn how to separate mixtures into pure substances. We will look at four useful methods. First we will study filtration to separate solids from liquids.
Filtration uses a filter paper to trap solid particles. The liquid that passes through is called the filtrate. This is useful for separating sand from water.

items: Step 2: Solid trapped by filter paper

explain.say: Evaporation is used to separate a dissolved solid from a liquid. We heat the mixture until only the solid remains. For example, we can recover salt from saltwater.
Distillation separates liquids with different boiling points. We boil the liquid and then cool the vapour back into a liquid. This is how we separate alcohol from water.

items: Step 3: Pure liquid collected in receiver

explain.say: Crystallisation is used to obtain pure solid crystals. We dissolve a substance in hot solvent and then cool it slowly. This allows pure crystals to form, like from copper sulfate.
In everyday life, we use distillation when we purify drinking water. Boiling the water and collecting the steam as liquid gives us clean water.

faq.q: When should I use filtration instead of evaporation?
faq.a: Use filtration when you want to separate a solid that does not dissolve in the liquid. Evaporation is for solids that dissolve.
asks: What is the difference between filtering and boiling off?
Can I filter salt out of water?
Do I boil the liquid first for filtration?

faq.q: What is the difference between distillation and simple evaporation?
faq.a: Evaporation leaves the solid behind, but distillation collects the liquid separately. Distillation is used when you need the liquid back.
asks: Why do I need a condenser for distillation?
Is distillation just boiling and cooling?
Can I distill something that doesn't boil?

faq.q: Can I use crystallisation to separate salt from water?
faq.a: Yes, but evaporation is often faster for just salt. Crystallisation is better when you want large, pure crystals of a substance.
asks: Is crystallisation the same as evaporation?
Do I need to cool it slowly for crystals?

faq.q: Are these techniques only for chemistry labs?
faq.a: No, these principles are used in many real-world processes. For example, making wine uses distillation.
asks: Do people use these at home?
Where else do I see these separation methods?

faq.q: What is the main difference between the techniques?
faq.a: Filtration separates by particle size, evaporation by boiling point, distillation by boiling point, and crystallisation by solubility changes.
asks: What property do these methods rely on?
Do I need heat for all of them?

facts: Filtration separates insoluble solids from liquids.
Evaporation leaves a solid residue behind in the container.
Distillation separates miscible liquids with different boiling points.
Crystallisation relies on the solubility of a substance changing with temperature.

quiz.say: To separate sand from a cup of water, which method should you use?
quiz.why: Filtration physically traps the solid sand while allowing the liquid water to pass through.

wrong.0: Evaporation would boil the water away, leaving the sand behind, which is not the goal.
wrong.1: Distillation is for separating liquids, not for separating a solid from a liquid.
wrong.2: Crystallisation is used to grow pure solid crystals from a solution, not to separate sand.

quiz.say: If you want to collect pure water from saltwater, what technique is best?
quiz.why: Distillation boils the water into steam, which is then cooled back into pure liquid water.

wrong.1: Evaporation would leave the salt behind, and you would lose the water vapor.
wrong.2: Filtration cannot separate dissolved salt from the water liquid.
wrong.3: Crystallisation would only give you solid salt crystals, not the liquid water.

quiz.say: A solution is cooled slowly to obtain large, pure crystals of sugar. This process is:
quiz.why: Cooling a saturated solution slowly encourages the formation of well-structured, pure crystals.

wrong.1: Evaporation is faster and might leave small, impure crystals or just residue.
wrong.2: Filtration only removes solid particles, not dissolved substances like sugar.
wrong.3: Distillation requires the substance to be volatile enough to boil.
